key_insight: CAMBY will investigate how brain network structure and function relate to persistent concussion symptoms in adolescents; it is not an AI or cancer drug discovery study.
clinical_relevance: Findings could inform future targeted neurostimulation trials for persistent concussion symptoms, but the study does not test a treatment.
method: Prospective observational study of adolescents aged 12–18 with a concussion history.
Collect MRI, MEG, and neuropsychological measures at least one month after concussion.
Compare persistent-symptom and recovered groups and examine relationships between brain networks and neuropsychological features.
evidence_signal: This protocol describes planned imaging and neuropsychological comparisons but reports no participant results or treatment outcomes.
watch_item: Observational associations cannot establish that brain network differences cause persistent symptoms or predict benefit from neurostimulation.
paper_title: Concussion, Attention, and Mental Health: A Brain Network Study in Youth (CAMBY) - Study Protocol
